Warm-Up — Quick Fire
Activation · Business Email Context
5–8 min
Q1 — T-S

How many emails do you send or read at work every day?

Q2 — S-S

Do you write emails in English at your job? What is difficult?

Q3 — Class

What is a good subject line for an email about a meeting? Give an example.

Q4 — T-S

Is email formal or informal at your company? When do you use WhatsApp instead?

TEACHER NOTE — Running the Warm-Up

Say: "Today we start Module 5 — Business Communication. Every professional sends emails. Today you will write one correctly in English." Q1 is a show-of-hands question. Q2 surfaces real anxiety about email — use it to validate: "It's normal to find this hard. After today it will be easier." For Q3, accept any attempt. Write two student subject lines on the board and discuss which is clearer.

⚡ QUICK WIN — 30 seconds
Say this out loud: "I'm writing to confirm our meeting on Friday." — That's a real business email opener. You already know all those words!

Module 5 Intro Video

2
Speaking Topic — Email Situations
Real context · Mónica Herrera · ConnectPro
8–10 min
T-S
Mónica Herrera is a sales manager at ConnectPro. She needs to write an email to confirm a client meeting. What information does the email need?
Think: date · time · place · topic
"The email needs: the date and time of the meeting, the location or the link for the video call, and the topic — for example, 'Q3 sales results.' A good subject line is also important: 'Meeting Confirmation — Friday, May 15th.'"
S-S
Partner A: You are Mónica. You want to confirm a meeting with a client for next Monday at 10 AM. Partner B: You are the client. Ask one question about the meeting.
Use: "I'm writing to confirm…" / "The meeting is on Monday at…"
A: "I'm writing to confirm our meeting on Monday at 10 AM. The meeting is about the new contract. Please let me know if you have any questions." B: "Thank you. Where is the meeting — in your office or online?"
Class
In your job, what situations need a formal email? Think of 3 real examples from your workplace.
Examples: absence notification / delivery confirmation / request for information
"I write formal emails when I: (1) confirm a delivery date with a supplier, (2) notify HR about a medical absence, and (3) request a purchase order approval from my manager."
TEACHER NOTE — Speaking Rounds

Round 1: Give students 30 seconds to think alone, then T-S open call. Round 2: pairs role-play for 2 min — walk the room. Round 3: class share — write the 3 email situations on the board and vote for the most common at their workplace. Common error: Students say "I am write" → correct immediately to "I am writing." This is the core phrase of the session.

Vocabulary — Business Email Words
12 key words · Click to hear · Flip cards
10 min
subject line
the title of an email
"Meeting Confirmation" is a clear subject line.
Suena: SUB-yect lain
greeting
the opening of an email (Dear / Hi)
Use "Dear" for formal emails to clients.
Suena: GRII-ting
attachment
a file sent with an email
Please find the report attached.
Suena: a-TACH-ment
sign-off
the closing of an email (Best regards)
Use "Kind regards" to close a professional email.
Suena: sain-OF
confirm
to say something is correct or agreed
Please confirm your attendance by Friday.
Suena: con-FERM
request
to ask for something formally
I request a copy of the invoice, please.
Suena: re-KUEST
forward
to send an email to another person
Can you forward this email to your manager?

reply
to answer an email
Please reply before 5 PM today.
Suena: re-PLAI
deadline
the last date to finish something
The deadline for the report is Thursday.
Suena: DED-lain
apology
saying sorry in writing
I would like to offer my apology for the delay.
Suena: a-PO-lo-yi
available
free, not busy
I am available on Monday at 10 AM.
Suena: a-VEI-la-bel
agenda
the list of topics for a meeting
Please send me the agenda before the meeting.
Suena: a-YEN-da
TEACHER NOTE — Pronunciation Focus

3 words to drill: (1) attachment — stress on the middle syllable: a-TACH-ment. (2) confirm — students often say CON-firm → correct to con-FERM. (3) available — 4 syllables: a-VEI-la-bel. Click each card to hear it. Use chorus repetition x3 before moving on.

🗣️ MICRO-SPEAKING
Say 3 of these words in a sentence about your real job. Example: "I receive 20 emails per day. I always confirm the deadline with my manager."

📋 Vocabulary Quiz — Email Words

TEACHER NOTE — Vocab Quiz Use

Run the quiz as a class on the projector first — students call out answers together. Then give 3 minutes for individual practice on their device. Badge b2 is awarded at 8+ correct. If students score low, return to the flip cards for a second round before moving on. False friend alert: "agenda" in Spanish is a planner/diary — in English, it means the list of topics for a meeting. Different!

4
Colloquial — Real Email English
4 phrases professionals actually use
5 min
"Got it."
A short way to say "I understood / I received your message." Used in replies to avoid long phrases. Example: "Got it. I'll send the report by 5 PM."
"On it."
Means "I am working on it / I will handle this." Confident and professional. Example: "Can you send the invoice? — On it, I'll have it to you in 10 minutes."
"Sounds good."
Agreement with a plan or suggestion. Friendly and positive. Example: "Meeting on Friday at 3 PM? — Sounds good, see you then."
"Thanks a lot."
Warmer than "Thank you." Used in semi-formal emails with colleagues you know. Example: "I received the documents. Thanks a lot for sending them so quickly."
TEACHER NOTE — Colloquial Drill

Read each phrase aloud with the group x2. Then play a quick substitution drill: Say a formal phrase → students respond with the colloquial version. Example: "I understand and will proceed." → Students: "Got it." / "I will work on this immediately." → "On it." These 4 phrases appear in real corporate English every day — tell students they can use them in email replies starting TODAY.

5
Grammar — Email Structure + Wh-Questions
Problem → Tool format
12–15 min
⚠️ REAL WORK SITUATION

Your manager says: "Send Mónica an email to confirm the meeting." You open your laptop. You write: "Hello Mónica meeting is on Friday 10 AM."

❌ This is incomplete. A professional email has structure. You need to know WHERE each part goes and HOW to start each sentence. That is the tool you will learn today.

Email Structure — The 5 Parts

PartEnglishA1.2 Example
1. Subject lineMeeting Confirmation / Request for InformationShort and clear. No verb needed.
2. GreetingDear Mónica, / Hi Carlos,"Dear" = formal. "Hi" = semi-formal.
3. Opening lineI'm writing to confirm / I'm writing to requestAlways state your purpose first.
4. BodyPlease find attached… / Could you send me…?One idea per sentence.
5. Sign-offBest regards, / Kind regards,Then: your name and title.

Wh-Questions in Emails

Wh-wordUseEmail example
Whatask about thingsWhat is the agenda for the meeting?
Whenask about timeWhen is the delivery scheduled?
Whereask about placeWhere is the meeting — your office or online?
Whoask about a personWho is the contact person for this order?
How manyask about quantityHow many copies do you need?
How longask about durationHow long is the meeting?
TEACHER NOTE — Grammar Delivery

Use the PROBLEM card to hook students — they have all felt this moment. Then reveal the table as the solution. Say: "Every professional email in English has these 5 parts. If you include them all, your email is correct." For Wh-questions: drill the pattern on the board — Wh-word + auxiliary (is/are/do/does) + subject + verb?. Write "When is the meeting?" and have students produce 3 more questions about a hypothetical work email.

Activity A — Quick Poll: Email or Not?

Is each item the correct part of a business email? Click True or False.

1. Subject line: "Hi, how are you? I hope you're well and the family too. Anyway I need to ask you something about the meeting on Friday..."

Subject lines must be short and direct: "Meeting Confirmation — Friday"

2. Opening line: "I'm writing to confirm our meeting on Thursday, March 20th at 2 PM."

✅ Perfect. States purpose + all details in one sentence.

3. Sign-off: "Bye! 👋"

Use: "Best regards," or "Kind regards," + your name and title.

4. Wh-question: "What is the agenda for tomorrow's meeting?"

✅ Correct structure: What + is + subject + phrase?
🗣️ MICRO-SPEAKING
Tell your partner: "I'm writing to…" and complete the sentence with a real reason from your job. You have 20 seconds each.

Activity B — Put the Email in Order

Drag the email parts into the correct order (1 = first, 5 = last).

  • ⠿Best regards, Mónica Herrera · Sales Manager
  • ⠿Dear Mr. Ramírez,
  • ⠿I'm writing to confirm our meeting on Friday, May 16th at 10 AM.
  • ⠿Meeting Confirmation — Friday, May 16th
  • ⠿Please let me know if you have any questions. I look forward to meeting you.
GT ORIGINAL — Error Patterns at A1.2

3 errors that appear every single class: (1) "I am write to you" → I am writing to you (present continuous, no shortcuts). (2) "Attached you find the report" → Please find the report attached. (3) "With kind regards" → Kind regards, (no "with"). Write these on the board and leave them up during Activity B.

6
Listening — A Business Email Read Aloud
Mónica Herrera · ConnectPro International · Guadalajara
8–10 min
Meeting Confirmation Email — ConnectPro International, Guadalajara
A1.2 · M5 · S1A · Voice: Katelyn (American English) · Speed: 0.80
ElevenLabs Script — ~155 words · ~58 seconds at 0.80

Hello. My name is Mónica Herrera, and I am the Sales Manager at ConnectPro International in Guadalajara. Today I want to read you a business email — a real one. Listen carefully.

Subject line: Meeting Confirmation — Thursday, May 22nd.

Dear Mr. Ochoa,

I am writing to confirm our meeting on Thursday, May 22nd at 3 PM. The meeting is in our office at Avenida Vallarta 1234, third floor, Conference Room B. The agenda has three topics: the Q2 sales report, the new client proposal, and the delivery schedule for June.

Please find the presentation attached. Could you send me your report before Wednesday? I need it to prepare the meeting.

I am available on Tuesday afternoon if you have any questions. Please do not hesitate to contact me.

Best regards,
Mónica Herrera
Sales Manager · ConnectPro International
Tel: +52 33 1234 5678

Comprehension — True or False

1. The meeting is on Thursday at 3 PM.

✅ Correct — Thursday, May 22nd at 3 PM.

2. The meeting has two topics on the agenda.

Three topics: Q2 report, new client proposal, and delivery schedule.

3. Mónica asks Mr. Ochoa to send his report before Wednesday.

✅ "Could you send me your report before Wednesday?"

4. The meeting is in a hotel meeting room.

The meeting is at ConnectPro's office, Avenida Vallarta 1234, third floor.

5. Mónica signs off with "Best regards."

✅ "Best regards, Mónica Herrera, Sales Manager."
🗣️ MICRO-SPEAKING
From memory: What is the subject line of Mónica's email? What does she ask Mr. Ochoa to do? Tell your partner in 2 sentences.
TEACHER NOTE — Listening Strategy

Play once without the script visible — students listen for gist. Then reveal the script and play again — students read along. T/F questions are done after the second listen. For advanced students in the group: ask them to identify the 5 parts of the email structure using the table from §5. This doubles as grammar review.

SP
Speaking Practice
6 guided questions · Pair and group discussion
10–12 min
T-S
What is a subject line? Give me one example from a real email you sent this week.
Grammar: "A subject line is…" / "For example: …"
S-S
How do you start a formal email to a client? And to a colleague you know well? What is the difference?
Use: "For a client, I use… / For a colleague, I use…"
S-S
Write a subject line for this situation: You need to tell your manager you can't come to work tomorrow because you are sick.
Think: short, clear, professional
Class
What questions do you write in English emails? Give one Wh-question you use at work.
Examples: What/When/Where/Who/How many/How long
S-S
Your partner asks you: "Could you confirm the meeting for next week?" Reply with a complete email response — at least 3 sentences.
Use: "I'm writing to confirm…" / "The meeting is on…" / "Best regards…"
Class
Challenge: Dictate a 3-sentence professional email to your partner. They type it on their phone. Include: subject line, opening, sign-off.
This is your speaking production challenge for today!
TEACHER NOTE — Speaking Practice Management

Use the timer for Q5 — pairs have 3 minutes to complete the mini email dictation. Walk the room. Collect 2-3 student emails and project them on the screen — analyze them as a class using the 5-part structure from §5. Which parts are there? Which are missing? This makes the grammar immediately visible and memorable. Celebrate students who include all 5 parts.

🎯 This Week at Work — Use These 3 Phrases
"I'm writing to confirm…"
Start any confirmation email with this phrase. Your boss will notice the professionalism immediately.
"Please find [X] attached."
Use when you send a document. This phrase is used in real corporate emails every day in the US, UK and Canada.
"Got it. On it."
Two words. Reply to any email in 2 seconds like a professional. Short, confident, clear.
7
Production — Write & Speak
Opinion Meter + Challenge
12–15 min
"Email is MORE professional than WhatsApp for all work communication."
Disagree50/50Agree
50%
TEACHER NOTE — Opinion Meter

All students vote simultaneously. Then ask 3 students to justify their position: "Why do you disagree?" — Use it as a springboard for real speaking production. The best argument usually comes from engineers who use WhatsApp for urgent factory floor issues. This leads naturally into discussing formal vs. informal register — great for the next session on corporate phone calls.

🏆 Final Challenge — Email Sprint

Situation: You are Carlos Ramírez, Operations Coordinator at Solaris Manufacturing in Celaya. Write a short email to your supplier to confirm a delivery on Tuesday, June 3rd at 9 AM. Include: subject line, greeting, 2-sentence body, sign-off with your name and title.

After the timer: 2-3 students read their emails aloud. Class gives feedback: "Did it have all 5 parts?"
